entries.tip: Never withhold a result to bait a counterclaim. Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it, or the moment someone challenges you, and keep your last will current. A result held back and then revealed after an opponent's claim looks retrofitted.

support.note: Judy, the real Sheriff, held back her Evil result on Erin and her will still said 'no results yet'. Town read her result as fabricated and hanged her 8-4.

entries.tip: When two Sheriff claimants call each other Evil, both results can be true: Executioners and Jesters read Evil. An early Day 2 Evil claim against someone who fights hard to survive may be an Executioner push. Don't hang on who sounded better. Wait a day or find a mechanical check; the delay is cheap.

support.note: Erin (Executioner) fake-claimed Sheriff with Evil on Judy. Judy's Evil result on Erin was real. Town hanged Judy anyway, giving Erin the win and a revenge kill on Alice.
Dave and Erin: don't execute on a single unverified result when a counterclaim exists. Carol's fake result muddied Alice's real one.

entries.tip: Fake-claim Sheriff early and report an Evil result on your target with a simple, believable reason. Leading first makes any later counterclaim from the target look reactionary.

support.note: Erin claimed she investigated Judy and got Evil ('last to speak, carbon-copy answer'). Judy was hanged and Erin won.

entries.tip: Assume the real holder of any role you fake-claim is alive, and that token counts can be checked. A Vanilla claim is unsafe if you hold tokens, so prepare a story that fits what a token check would show. If your claim is broken, don't switch to another power role a living player can counterclaim. Never claim a role that a living Lookout or Tracker result can contradict.

support.note: Frank fake-claimed Medic after Mallory's Lookout saw him visit Dave. That made a 1v1 against the real Medic Grace, and Carol shot Frank.
Moderator and Niaj: both of Carol's and Niaj's fake claims collapsed against living real role holders.
Moderator: Mallory's fake Vigilante claim was instantly counterclaimed by Niaj, and she was shot that night.
Frank: Grace's audit showed his fake Surveyor claim at 0 tokens. Ivan's gift didn't help, because it was thrown away.

history.old: Assume the real holder of any role you fake-claim is alive and will post the same night history. Never claim a role (especially Medic) that a living Lookout or Tracker result can contradict. Prefer Vanilla or a claim no living player can check, or kill the info role first.
history.note: Heidi's audit showed Carol held 1 token, which broke her Vanilla claim. Carol switched to Archivist and the real Archivist Erin counterclaimed. Niaj switched from Vanilla to Medic and lost to the real Medic Judy plus Frank's track showing he never visited.

entries.tip: Keep your votes consistent with your stated reads. Accusing someone and then voting No or Innocent on them is exactly the contradiction Vigilantes shoot. Village: scan for these read/vote mismatches.

support.note: Frank called Grace the Katana attacker, then voted No on her nomination. Carol shot him that night, citing it in her will.
Bob, Erin and Ivan: the read/vote mismatches around Carol and Mallory drove the discussion to concrete points.

entries.tip: Every Yakuza must submit their agreed night action and Katana vote every night. Confirm the exact holder and target in night chat. With two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. Make plans that still work if one teammate does nothing.

support.note: Ivan never acted on N1-N4 and cast no Katana vote on N4, so Bob's kill on Carol failed. Blocking Grace on N1 or N2 would likely have landed kills.
Alice and Carol: the team confirmed holder and target each night, and no attack was lost to a missed vote.
Alice, Bob, Grace, Mallory and the moderator: holder and target were confirmed every night, including at 2 alive, and every Katana attack resolved.

entries.tip: Hold your shots until you have a mechanical lead: a claim conflict, a flipped Yakuza's vote or PM partners, or votes that clearly contradict the player's own stated reads. Never shoot on a soft behavioral read or on odd questions; the player may hold hidden info. A misfire costs as much as a mislynch and can hand Yakuza parity. Use Basic shots to save tokens, and claim only after your shots flip Yakuza.

support.note: Carol made three Basic shots, all on Yakuza (Frank, Bob, Ivan), each based on vote inconsistencies. She claimed on Day 5.
Erin held her shots on N1-N2, then used one Basic shot on Dave, the triangle starter, who flipped Fabricator. She later shot Heidi with Standard.

against.note: Alice: Niaj followed the 'stay hidden and shoot' advice and shot Erin, the Surveyor, on a behavioral read. That cost the town a power role and opened space for Mallory's fake Vigilante claim.

history.old: Stay hidden and spend Basic shots on players whose votes contradict their own stated reads, which saves tokens for more targets. Claim publicly only after your shots flip Yakuza, then use that credibility to lead the town.
history.note: Moderator, Niaj, Carol, Heidi, Erin and Ivan: Niaj's N2 Basic shot on Surveyor Erin, a 'bad read' whose votes matched her lean, put the town at 4v3 under a Ballot Stuffer lock.

entries.tip: Protect the likeliest Katana targets: vocal analysts early, then claimed investigators. Free Standard protection used night after night can carry the town.

support.note: Grace protected Alice on N1 and Tracker Dave on N2, and both Katana attacks failed.
Dave: never skip N1 protection. Standard Defense stops a Katana, and he was killed (and blocked) on N1.
Frank protected claimed Sheriff Alice every night and stopped the N1 Katana.
Judy protected from N1. She saved Heidi on N1 and Erin on N6, which secured the 3-1 endgame.

entries.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action or alignment. A track or watch cannot tell protection from framing or a Katana attack. A Lookout sees only visitors to their target, so watching the Katana holder shows nothing about the holder's attack. Killing an attacker at night does not cancel their attack that same night.

support.note: Carol, Mallory and Grace all stressed this during the Medic-claim dispute over visits to Dave.
On N4, Erin's shot and Heidi's Katana resolved simultaneously, and they traded lives.
Moderator, Mallory and Dave: Niaj's shot killed Mallory even though the Katana killed Niaj that same night, and the Yakuza planned around it.

history.old: A visit shows a destination, not an action or alignment. A track or watch cannot tell protection from framing or a Katana attack. Also, killing an attacker at night does not cancel their attack that same night.
history.note: Heidi wrongly called Erin's 'nobody visited Grace' a contradiction of Grace holding the Katana, which helped hang the real Lookout.

entries.tip: You get no feedback on whether your protection worked. Never claim you 'saw' or confirmed a save. Say your protection is consistent with the target's survival.

support.note: Alice and Grace both flagged overclaiming during the Medic dispute.
Judy never claimed a confirmed save, and her claim stayed credible through two trials. Bob and the moderator agreed.

entries.tip: Keep hostile Neutrals (SK, Arsonist) in the suspect pool even after Yakuza die. A Not Evil Sheriff result or a Vanilla claim doesn't clear them. A failed attack with no block notice can mean innate Defense, not just a Medic.

support.note: Niaj (Arsonist) sat as a Vanilla claim into the final three.
Heidi (Arsonist) survived the N5 Katana with no credible Medic claim, then switched from 'VV thanked a Medic' to 'Medic' on trial. Carol, Alice and Olivia all read this as innate Defense.

entries.tip: Ignite as soon as 3 or more living players are doused, or the moment you come under suspicion. Every night spent dousing is a night the town can hang you first. Ignite is Astral: trap-safe and invisible to Fortune Teller counts. Douse players likely to survive, not today's lynch targets, and count living douses before each night.

support.note: Niaj doused five players over five nights, never ignited, and was hanged at three alive.

history.old: Don't douse forever. Ignite once your douses would swing the endgame. Douse players likely to stay alive, not today's lynch targets. Before each night, count living players against your living douses.
history.note: Heidi had doused all three living Yakuza by N5, doused again instead of igniting, and was hanged on D6. One ignite would have wiped out the Yakuza. Heidi and the moderator.

entries.tip: Ignite is a Strong Astral attack: invisible to Lookout and Tracker, but it fails against Strong Defense (e.g. a Medic spending tokens on themselves). Douse is a normal visit, so don't douse a player a Tracker has publicly committed to tracking.

support.note: Niaj's own analysis.

entries.tip: As a solo killer, don't ride a no-info Vanilla claim into the final three opposite cross-confirmed Village roles. Build checkable reads early and push real doubt between the confirmed players while you still can. At three alive, two Yes votes hang you.

support.note: Niaj refused to make any case at three alive and Dave and Grace hanged him 2-1.

entries.tip: Right after a teammate flips, don't lead a push on a quiet Villager who argued against that teammate. A Vigilante reads it as revenge for the flipped player.

support.note: Bob drove Heidi's hang the day after Frank flipped. Heidi was Vanilla, and Carol shot Bob that night citing the push.

entries.tip: Don't vote as a block with a doomed teammate; vote Guilty with the town. First do the vote math in night chat, though. If your team's Innocent votes (plus a Ballot Stuffer's doubled vote) can stop the execution, defend them: an exposed teammate saved beats a clean record. Plan the whole team's votes across trials in advance, because lone Innocent votes on a teammate who later flips become the case against you.

support.note: Bob and Ivan were later scrutinized over votes that sided with exposed teammates.
Grace: Carol's paired Innocent votes alongside Bob and Grace became the main evidence against her.
Dave, Bob and Heidi all voted Guilty on Alice on D3 while every villager voted Innocent. After Dave's flip, Bob was hanged on that vote record.
Moderator, Alice, Bob, Frank and Grace: Mallory's repeated Innocent votes on flipped Yakuza got her hanged, while Alice's Guilty votes protected her.
Alice and Grace: the team voted Guilty with the town on Frank and stayed blended, keeping a clean record.
Olivia: her No vote on Frank's nomination marked her for the rest of the game. Bob voted Yes and Guilty on Frank and stayed unsuspected until the end. The rule applies to nomination votes too.

against.note: Moderator: Grace was exposed but not doomed, because the doubled vote allowed a 4-4 tie. Bob and Mallory chose not to bus her and saved her; bussing would have cost the win.

history.old: Don't vote as a block with an exposed teammate. Spread your votes, and sometimes vote with town against a doomed teammate to protect your own read.
history.note: Mallory was the only voter besides Carol to vote Innocent at Carol's execution, then voted Innocent on Niaj, and was hanged on D6. Alice voted Guilty on both and survived to the final day. Niaj noted that distancing must be coordinated across trials.

history.old: Don't vote as a block with an exposed teammate. Once a teammate is clearly doomed, vote Guilty with the town. Plan the whole team's vote record across trials in night chat rather than improvising each trial, because lone Innocent votes on a teammate who later flips become the main case against you.
history.note: Moderator, Bob and Mallory: on D3 Grace was saved 4-4 by Innocent votes plus a stuffed vote. In earlier games, bussing doomed teammates protected the survivors.

entries.tip: While the Vigilante is unidentified and has shots left, prioritize killing the likeliest Vigilante. Each Vigilante shot on a Yakuza costs you more than any info role does.

support.note: Carol's shots killed three Yakuza. She was only killed on N5, after her last shot.

entries.tip: When a Lookout or Tracker is publicly active, give the Katana to a member with no claimed role and no reason to visit. Kill or block the info role first.

support.note: Frank's visit to Dave was seen by Mallory and became the main evidence against him.
Niaj: Frank was killed the night he claimed Tracker, and the Katana stayed with unclaimed members.

entries.tip: Keep your last will matching your current public claim every day. A will that contradicts your claim (e.g. Vanilla vs Medic) proves the lie when you die.

support.note: Frank's reflection after his flip.

entries.tip: Weigh contradictions between a player's own accepted premises or claimed knowledge far above awkward wording or delays. Ask explicitly which premise they reject. Before a hang, name what separates a lie from an honest mistake, a frame or a Roleplayer.

support.note: Mallory and Carol used Frank's conflicting premises about visitors to Dave to resolve the Medic dispute.
At 4 alive, Erin's consistent Lookout claim was hanged over a PM-direction slip while Carol (Yakuza) survived. That mislynch lost the game.
Dave, Heidi and Grace: correcting false 'contradictions' (optional Medic actions, a Tracker seeing visits rather than actions) kept true claims alive.
Ivan, Frank and Niaj: premise checks separated honest slips from lies. Dave's Roleplayer flip was correctly not read as deliberate deception.

against.note: Heidi: the town still treated Frank's corrected timeline slip as a tell and hanged him. The tip didn't stop the misapplication.

entries.tip: Watch likely visit targets (exposed investigators, probable kill targets) so you can catch both attacker and protector. Put your strongest contradiction into your will before a dangerous night, and share key private evidence promptly.

support.note: Mallory's N2 watch on Dave caught both Frank and Grace and set up the Medic counterclaim.

entries.tip: Track players who claim night actions, so a mismatch is informative. Avoid tracking the same player twice in a row, since a no-visit result on a stay-home Yakuza tells you little.

support.note: Heidi's analysis. Dave's tracks confirmed Mallory's and Grace's claims.

entries.tip: Trackers and Lookouts can announce tonight's target at the end of the day. This commits you before results exist, so your reports can't look retrofitted, and your death becomes verifiable info.

support.note: Alice's suggestion. Thin evidence.

against.note: Carol announced her watch on Heidi and was killed on N2. Alice's announced targets got her blocked every night. Six players and the moderator called public target announcements harmful.

entries.tip: Settle duplicate claims with independent corroboration (a Lookout or Tracker result confirming the same destination), not repetition or speaking style. Build a positive case for each claimant before a flip reveals the answer.

support.note: Judy, Niaj and Heidi all noted this. Mallory's and Dave's results were what resolved Grace vs Frank.

entries.tip: Ask every living player to name a strongest suspect with reasoning each day, so there is a record to check against later flips. But a named lean is a record, not evidence. Several players echoing the same soft lean add up to nothing, and Yakuza will nominate the pile-on target 'to hear a defense'. Never let a stack of leans become a Guilty vote.

support.note: Alice's lesson. Bob's four days of 'no nomination' followed by a sudden pivot was the tell.
Dave: long rounds of 'no nomination from me' let the Yakuza pick off Village roles. Name a concrete behavior and set a deadline.
Grace: stated daily reads made the later voting patterns easy to compare.
Erin: the named reads exposed inconsistencies, e.g. Alice's lean checked against her Guilty vote.

against.note: Moderator: forced daily leans piled onto Frank, and Grace (Yakuza) nominated him 'to hear a defense'. Vanilla Frank was hanged 6-5.

history.old: Ask every living player to name a strongest suspect with reasoning each day, even if they won't nominate. Repeated 'no case' answers give evil free cover, while named reads create a record to check against later flips.
history.note: Moderator, Frank, Bob and Erin: the leans helped later analysis, but they stacked into the D2 mislynch of Vanilla Frank and gave Yakuza cover.

entries.tip: Scrutinize a player who stays silent for days and then suddenly produces a concrete accusation right as the board changes. The timing of the pivot is the signal.

support.note: Bob went from four days of 'no nomination' to pushing Heidi right after Frank flipped.
Ivan and Mallory: the timing of Carol's late Archivist claim and Mallory's will drew useful scrutiny.

against.note: Frank: Ivan's late Oracle claim was true, and suspicion over its timing helped get him hanged. Vote patterns, not timing, found the Yakuza.

entries.tip: Keep a running ledger of every trial vote and announced total, plus each night's deaths, blocks and reported visits. Revisit it after every flip, and cross-check claims against it daily.

support.note: Heidi lost her trial partly because she couldn't cite the vote-symmetry data that would have countered Bob.
Dave, Ivan and Niaj: the vote ledger and PM record correctly identified the Bob/Mallory/Grace bloc, though too late.

history.old: Keep a running tally of every trial vote and every position change, so you can cite vote data crisply when you are accused.
history.note: Dave, Judy and Erin: Judy's and Niaj's competing Medic claims stayed open for days because nobody tracked blocks and visits, while the vote ledger exposed Mallory.

entries.tip: On Night 1, investigate a prominent player or one likely to make a claim, and plan to disclose the result right away. An early public result is worth more than a hidden one.

support.note: Judy's reflection.

entries.tip: Since private messages are publicly visible, briefly summarize their content in public. Unexplained PM clusters right after claims or votes became a main source of suspicion.

support.note: Erin, Grace and Dave all noted the PM graph being used as evidence.
Erin and Ivan: Erin's audit-request PM to Heidi became a public point of suspicion.

entries.tip: Before accusing anyone from public data, re-check the ledger: who sent each private message (not just who received it), each vote, and the exact wording of role results. One reversed fact can discredit an otherwise true claimant.

support.note: Six players and the moderator flagged this. Erin, the real Lookout, reversed who messaged Carol, lost credibility and was hanged 3-1.

entries.tip: The Katana holder appears Not Evil to a Sheriff checking them that same night. A Not Evil result on a suspected attacker clears nothing. Say so when you post it.

support.note: Alice's reflection on the Katana exception.
Alice got Not Evil on Heidi on N4 because Heidi held the Katana, though Heidi was Yakuza.
Mallory and Carol: Alice matched Good Ivan in Carol's Seer comparison only because Alice held the Katana that night.

entries.tip: Don't hint at your own power role or its tokens on Day 1, especially a protective one or a Veteran. Investigators should still post results publicly once they matter, not only in a will that may come too late. When a Ritualist may be alive, never name another living player's exact role in your will or in public; write 'one of X/Y holds info, ask them'.

support.note: Dave twice said he was 'holding my Medic tokens'. The Yakuza blocked and killed him on N1.
Frank claimed Medic privately and Alice acknowledged it in public on D3. The Yakuza killed Frank that night.
Frank held his Tracker claim until D4 and tracked unblocked until then. Bob agreed.
Judy: as a quiet Veteran she drew the Katana on N2 and her alert killed Alice.
Carol said her action 'doesn't visit'. The Yakuza chat repeatedly said 'avoid Carol (possible Veteran)'. Her three alerts caught nobody, and she was hanged with 0 tokens.

against.note: Erin: hiding early made late claims look retrofitted. Her example was Yakuza Carol's Vanilla lie, so this is weak evidence against.
Moderator: Erin kept her Surveyor result for her will, and it effectively named Carol as Seer. With a Ritualist alive, that became a guaranteed kill on Carol.

history.old: Don't hint at a power role or its tokens on Day 1, especially a protective one. It marks you as the first kill. Put the info in your last will instead.
history.note: Moderator, Erin and Judy: hiding helped Veteran Judy, but Erin's will-only Surveyor result came too late and pointed the Ritualist at Carol.

entries.tip: Never speak publicly from your hidden perspective. Say 'died to a Katana', never 'my Katana'. Agree on public wording in night chat.

support.note: Grace opened Day 2 with 'Dave died to my Katana' and Heidi shot her that night with one Basic token. Bob and Dave flagged it too.

entries.tip: After a Yakuza flips, your top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination or argued to delay the hang, voted Innocent alongside them, or exchanged PMs with them. A Guilty vote once the trial is clearly lost is cheap cover. Players who were merely fooled into vouching for the fake's results rank lower. Weigh these hard links above unverifiable late claims (e.g. Roleplayer) and above new theories built on disputed counts. Track voting blocs across trials.

support.note: Carol voted Innocent on Bob with Bob and Grace, and both had messaged her. Her post-hoc Roleplayer claim got her acquitted, and the Village lost.
Moderator, Heidi, Judy, Dave, Grace and Carol: Mallory's Innocent votes on Carol and Niaj, both of whom flipped Yakuza, built the case that hanged her.

history.old: In the endgame, weigh hard links to flipped Yakuza (Innocent votes alongside them on key trials, PMs from them) above an unverifiable late claim like Roleplayer. Track voting blocs across trials.
history.note: Only Alice and Olivia voted No on Frank's nomination, then voted Guilty. Both were Yakuza. Ivan pointed this out on D5, but the town hanged Ivan instead. Carol, Grace, Judy, Ivan, Niaj and the moderator all made this point.

entries.tip: If you must fake-claim, build it on info your team created, e.g. a Roleplayer or Sheriff 'Evil' result on your Fabricator's frame target. That also explains your suspicious votes. Then pivot pressure onto whoever voted Guilty on you.

support.note: Carol claimed Roleplayer with 'Alice = Evil', matching Bob's N1 frame. She was acquitted, then nominated and hanged Erin, the sole Guilty voter.

entries.tip: Pair your block with the Katana kill on the same target, or block the likeliest Vigilante or protector. If you also hold the Katana, block the Vigilante every night; you are block-immune, so you can't be stopped.

support.note: Carol blocked Dave as he was killed on N1, then blocked Heidi on N3-N4 while killing Frank and Heidi.

entries.tip: Never announce when or whom you will shoot while a role-blocker may be alive. Telegraphing lets evil block or kill you first.

support.note: Heidi said 'I'm deciding tonight' on Day 4. Carol blocked and then killed her.

entries.tip: Treat the nomination and trial votes as separate decisions, unless a Clerk may hold an unused rig token. In that case a passed nomination can mean execution whatever the trial vote: vote Yes only on someone you'd accept dying, and vote No at the nomination if you are a likely target. Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in their claims, votes or a mechanical result, and say why an innocent explanation no longer fits. Echoed concerns and corrected slips are not new evidence. A nominator who 'just wants to hear a defense' has given no case.

support.note: Frank's reflection.
Heidi: say so when a Yes vote is only to hear someone out, and judge guilt fresh at the verdict.
Ivan: separating the nomination from the execution decision kept him voting Innocent on Frank, who flipped Vanilla.

history.old: Treat the nomination and trial votes as separate decisions. Yes only puts someone on trial; vote Guilty only after their defense, if the evidence supports execution.
history.note: Moderator, Ivan, Frank, Carol, Heidi and Erin: Frank was hanged 6-5 on stacked leans and a corrected timeline slip after Grace (Yakuza) nominated him 'to hear a defense'.

history.old: Treat the nomination and trial votes as separate decisions. Yes only puts someone on trial. Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in their own claims, votes or a mechanical result, and say why an innocent explanation no longer fits. Echoed concerns and corrected slips are not new evidence. A nominator who says they 'just want to hear a defense' has given no case.
history.note: Heidi was executed through Bob's rig on D6 despite a 4-3 Innocent vote. Mallory, Niaj, Heidi and Grace all said a Yes vote should be treated as Guilty when a rig is possible.

entries.tip: Investigators (Sheriff, Lookout, Tracker): never announce tonight's target in public. Post only resolved results. An announced target tells the Pharmacist whom to block and tells the Katana where to strike or what to avoid.

support.note: Alice announced checks on Dave and then Heidi, and Bob blocked her every night. Carol announced a watch on Heidi, so the Yakuza moved the Katana to Dave and killed Carol on N2. Carol, Erin, Grace, Frank and Alice all reported this.
Judy publicly told Niaj to shoot Mallory, and the Katana killed Niaj that night.
Grace: announcing her audit plan told the Yakuza to kill her that night, and the result died with her.

entries.tip: Don't send private messages to teammates on Day 1. Plan in night chat. If you must DM, also message villagers, and never all repeat the same public explanation for your DMs. A visible PM triangle becomes the town's lead for the whole game.

support.note: Dave DMed Bob and Heidi repeatedly, and Bob and Heidi repeated his 'check-ins' excuse. The 'Dave/Bob/Heidi triangle' was cited all game and appeared in Carol's and Frank's wills.
Grace: Mallory and Bob PMed each other on D3 after voting Innocent on Grace, and Carol cited it as a tell.

entries.tip: Map who starts PM clusters and who co-nominates. If the same few players DM each other early and then push the same nomination with no new information, treat them as a likely Yakuza bloc. Once one of them flips, use the shared vote record against the others.

support.note: Alice, Carol and Grace tracked the Dave/Bob/Heidi triangle and their joint push on Alice. After Dave flipped, Bob was hanged 4-1 on the vote record.
Frank and Grace: the Carol/Judy/Niaj bloc that voted Yes on Bob kept resurfacing as an alignment signal.
Niaj and Ivan: the Mallory-Bob PM pair after their joint Innocent votes on Grace correctly marked the Yakuza bloc.
Mallory, Judy and Erin: the three Yakuza voted as a bloc on every trial from D5 on, with near-identical Guilty lines. The town noticed too late.

entries.tip: Save the forge token for a night your target is actually likely to die (e.g. the Katana target when no protector is suspected). Never put a fake role in your own will that your death reveal will disprove; it also discredits teammates making the same claim.

support.note: Dave spent his forge on N1 on Alice, but Medic Frank protected her. Dave's own 'Vanilla' will was exposed by his Fabricator flip, which made Bob's identical Vanilla claim easy to reject.

entries.tip: Treat a power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack, or who is role-blocked night after night, as likely real. Evil rarely spends its blocker and Katana on a fake.

support.note: Alice survived the N1 Katana and was blocked every night. Grace and Frank read this as the Yakuza hunting a real Sheriff and kept her alive.
Grace: Judy, who was blocked on N4-N5, was the real Medic.
Moderator, Erin and Frank: Judy survived the Katana and Alice died to a Veteran, so the claim was accepted at once and anchored the D3 role count.

entries.tip: Don't vote Guilty on an investigator just because they have no results. A blocked night produces nothing. Require a concrete contradiction, and be wary of a pair or trio pushing a trial with no new info.

support.note: The Yakuza trio pushed Alice to trial on D3 over her empty results; Bob had blocked her every night. Alice, Carol, Frank and Grace all flagged this.

entries.tip: After a failed Katana attack, assume the target is protected or has innate Defense. Don't retry blindly; kill or block the likely protector first. If no credible Medic is claimed, the survivor probably has their own Defense (Arsonist/SK Standard, Jester/Executioner Basic). Push them to the gallows (a rig works) instead of spending more night kills, which also looks pro-town.

support.note: The N1 Katana on Alice failed to Frank's protection. Heidi's reflection.
Heidi survived the N1 Katana to Judy's protection. The Yakuza switched targets, then blocked Judy on N4-N5 and landed kills. Alice, Carol, Niaj and the moderator all reported this helped.
Bob, Grace and Ivan: after Judy's alert killed Alice, the Yakuza never revisited Judy and switched to Niaj and Heidi.

history.old: After a failed Katana attack, assume the target is protected or has innate Defense. Don't retry the same target blindly; kill or block the likely protector first.
history.note: Alice and Olivia: the Katana failed on Heidi on N5, so the Yakuza hanged her through the rig on D6.

entries.tip: In the endgame, don't send the Katana at the player the Medic publicly claims to guard. Block or kill the Medic, or hit an unprotected target.

support.note: On N6 Alice attacked Erin, whom Judy had publicly claimed protecting. Judy protected her again, the attack failed, and the Village reached a 3-1 final day.

entries.tip: Get the mechanics right before calling something a contradiction. Night actions are optional unless a role says 'must'. Two players can claim the same role unless the rules make it unique. Count living players as of the right moment. A false 'contradiction' costs the accuser credibility.

support.note: Erin claimed a Medic must act every night, was corrected, and was later tried. Mallory's archive miscount was itself wrong. Bob, Dave, Heidi, Judy and Grace said the same.
Ivan, Dave and Judy: checking deadlines, claim timing and the archive count (N=9, 6 roles) against 8 votes from 7 voters exposed the Ballot Stuffer.

entries.tip: When announced trial totals don't match the revealed votes, record which side got the extra vote in each trial. Then find the one player whose votes line up with every manipulation, and combine that with any token or claim evidence before hanging.

support.note: Heidi saw an extra Innocent at Carol's trial and an extra Guilty at Ivan's, matching Carol's own votes, plus Carol's 1-token audit. Carol was hanged and flipped Ballot Stuffer. Frank, Erin, Dave and Judy agreed.
Judy and Ivan: the 8-vote total from 7 voters proved a Ballot Stuffer, confirmed the archive entry and located the stuffer among the Innocent voters.

entries.tip: Never name living teammates in your last will. Write it as a plausible Village player would.

support.note: Mallory's will said 'Alice is our Grunt', and that was the whole case that hanged Alice on D7. Frank and Alice noted it too.

entries.tip: Don't hang a power-role claimant just because the claim came late or is hard to verify, especially when the result fits the accused's own admissions. Before voting, ask who is pushing the trial and who benefits.

support.note: Ivan's true Oracle result (Niaj is not Vanilla) was answered with a Yakuza-led nomination by Alice and a doubled vote. Ivan was hanged, the Village's worst mistake.
Judy led the hang of Ivan, who had a coherent, checkable claim, on her own unverifiable count inference. It cost a villager and her credibility.

entries.tip: Combine public partial-role results with your private knowledge of your team to locate Neutrals and other threats, then kill them.

support.note: Dave's survey of Alice/Bob/Carol revealed a Vulture. Alice and Carol were Yakuza, so the Yakuza killed Bob, the Vulture, on N3.

entries.tip: A will that names a living player is a lead, not a verdict. Check the named player's own vote record and claims before hanging on it the same day.

support.note: Grace and Mallory: the case on Alice came from Mallory's will alone. It was correct this time, but thin evidence.

entries.tip: A clean token is spent even if the target survives. Clean only when the kill is near-certain (a target with no possible Defense and no likely protector), or when the target's will would expose something critical, such as a puppeting notice or an investigator's results. Never clean a target whose survival is in doubt.

support.note: Niaj's reflection.

history.old: Save your clean token for a kill that is likely to land. A clean only hides the role and will of someone who dies; it doesn't help an attack succeed, and it is wasted if the target survives.
history.note: Alice: the clean on Heidi was wasted against her Arsonist Defense. The clean on Niaj hid his puppet will and secured the win.

entries.tip: Log every protection target and any tokens spent in your will each day. A complete record lets others check your claim against Tracker results if a counterclaim appears.

support.note: Frank: the Judy vs Niaj Medic dispute was settled by matching Judy's claimed visits against his track.

entries.tip: While a Ritualist may be alive with tokens, every exact-role claim (Seer, Archivist, Eavesdropper) is a near-certain extra kill on top of the Katana. A living Diviner also feeds it exact roles, and a Wiretap reads private claims. Survey or archive results can pin a survivor's role indirectly. Claim only when it changes a vote, and expect the claimant to die that night.

support.note: Moderator, Judy, Dave and Mallory: Bob killed Ivan (via a Diviner check) and Carol (via Erin's will and her claim) with unannounced Ritualist guesses.

entries.tip: Chain exact-role info into Ritualist guesses: Diviner or Mortician results, Wiretap-read claims and public role claims give 100% guesses that never out the Ritualist. The Katana stays free for a second kill the same night. Save Ritualist tokens for confirmed investigators.

support.note: Moderator, Bob and Grace: Alice's N1 Diviner check on Ivan led to Bob's N2 kill, and Carol's claim led to the N3 kill. Both nights were double kills.

entries.tip: Give the Katana to the member whose own role matters least (Wiretap, Grunt), not your Diviner or other info source. Don't attack an unclaimed, confident, vocal organizer who may be an alerting Veteran. If you must hit one, have the Diviner give the holder Strong Defense (it beats the Veteran's Strong attack), or use an Astral Ritualist guess.

support.note: Moderator, Alice and Bob: Alice, the Diviner, held the Katana on N2, attacked Judy and died to her Veteran alert while Grace (Wiretap) sat idle.
Frank divined Bob, the Katana holder, on N3 for Strong Defense against a possible trap.

entries.tip: Do the trial math in night chat. Spend a token on the night your team gets close to half: a doubled Innocent vote makes trials need more Guilty than the Village has (e.g. 7 alive means 8 counted, so 5 Guilty are needed). That blocks every execution, even of an exposed teammate. Nomination votes aren't doubled.

support.note: Moderator, Mallory and Bob: Mallory's N2 token turned D3 into a 4-4 lock, and the exposed Grace survived.

entries.tip: When a trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists. Recompute the threshold at once (count the extra vote) and see whether any trial can still pass. If evil is near half with the stuffer, hangs are impossible: kill the stuffer or the evil bloc at night, and act on mechanical deductions before parity arrives. Count evil's kills per night (Katana + Ritualist + misfires), not just heads.

support.note: Judy, Ivan, Niaj, Heidi, Frank, Carol and Dave: at 4v3 with a stuffed vote, every D3 trial tied 4-4. Then the Katana plus Ritualist took two Villagers a night.

entries.tip: Combine an Archivist or Surveyor role list with flips and claims to rule out roles. If the Village Vanilla and power slots are accounted for, extra Vanilla claims or duplicate power claims are fake. Corroborating one entry (e.g. a stuffed vote proving the Ballot Stuffer) doesn't verify the whole list, so keep the deductions conditional and account for unsampled roles.

support.note: Moderator, Niaj, Judy, Dave and Ivan: Heidi's archive plus the claims exposed Bob's and Grace's fake Vanilla claims and Mallory's fake Vigilante claim, but only after the vote math was lost.

entries.tip: Agree the team's claim set in night chat. Never have two or more members claim Vanilla in a power-heavy setup; one archive list or role count can prove there is no Vanilla slot left and expose all of them at once. Spread claims over plausible unchecked roles, or stay unclaimed.

support.note: Alice, Bob and Frank: Bob's and Grace's Vanilla claims were both broken by Heidi's archive count.

entries.tip: Plan the endgame around exact vote math. Parity doesn't end the game. At 2v2, vote No on every nomination (none can reach a majority), kill one villager at night, then nominate and hang the last at 2-1. Before risky night trades, pre-agree exactly whom the survivors kill and how they vote.

support.note: Bob, Grace and Mallory: after the N3 trade (Niaj and Mallory dead), the pair blocked nominations, killed Heidi and hanged Judy 2-1.
Bob and Frank: at 3v2 the Yakuza stopped arguing, hanged Carol and killed Judy.

entries.tip: Never visit a revealed or suspected Veteran at night, and don't trust public claims that their alert tokens are spent. Kill the other villagers and hang the Veteran once you control the vote; hanging bypasses alerts.

support.note: Mallory, Bob, Grace and Ivan: after Alice died to Judy's alert, the Yakuza never visited Judy again and hanged her on D5.
The Yakuza avoided Carol (suspected Veteran) at night and hanged her at 5 alive.

entries.tip: Once you claim Veteran publicly, Yakuza will avoid you, so later alerts are mostly wasted. Claim when it confirms a kill or saves a lynch, ideally after your best alerts are used. If you claim, don't reveal how many tokens you have left; it tells evil when you are safe to visit.

support.note: Judy: her N2 alert killed Alice. After her claim, the Yakuza stayed away and hanged her instead.

entries.tip: Before nominating a soft-lean player, ask whether they could be a hidden info role. A trial forces their claim, and an Archivist or Seer claim mid-game can expose your whole lineup. Kill them quietly at night instead.

support.note: Alice: Heidi's archive came out under trial pressure on D3 and exposed Bob, Grace and Mallory.

entries.tip: If a Yakuza fake-claims your role first, counterclaim immediately with details only the real holder has (token count, shot reasoning), and put the claim in your will. A late counterclaim reads as an echo.

support.note: Niaj: Mallory's copied Vigilante claim muddied his identity until role-count math resolved it.

entries.tip: Choose targets who will likely survive the next Day and send private messages, not just today's suspect. You and your target must both be alive and there must be PM traffic. An empty record clears nobody.

support.note: Ivan's reflection; he was killed by the Ritualist on N2 before he could use his results.

entries.tip: Stay quiet and never hint publicly that a Wiretap exists. The Village's own fear of a Wiretap often shuts down PM evidence for you. Hold the Katana yourself when the team needs a low-value holder.

support.note: Grace: the town's 'no PMs because of Wiretap' warning killed PM evidence. Her teammates' PMs, not her, were the risk.

entries.tip: Fortune Teller numbers are unordered. One counts players visited; the other counts players who visited someone ELSE, so self-targets are excluded. One visitor can cover two targets, e.g. a Katana holder who also uses their own action. Equal numbers therefore don't prove nobody was double-visited. Before using a count, list every way it could fit: a holder acting twice, Ex-Con random visits, Arsonist douses, self-protects, and players who switched from a 'plan' in their will. A count that doesn't fit is weak evidence. Never hang on it alone, least of all against a claim backed by an exact-role check or a flip.

support.note: Frank held the Katana on N2, attacked Grace and divined Mallory, giving 6&6. Judy read that as 'no double visits', ruled out Ivan's real token visit, and the town hanged Ivan, the real Philanthropist. Judy, Ivan, Frank, Bob, Carol, Dave, Erin, Niaj and the moderator all reported this.

entries.tip: When a Clerk rig is announced, the Yakuza wanted that nominee dead. Treat the nominator, the players who pushed the nomination and every Guilty voter on that trial as prime suspects, and hang from that group next. Don't drift back to old suspects.

support.note: Dave, Erin and Niaj: the D6 rig on Heidi pointed at the Yakuza bloc, but the town never followed it up and lost at 3v2.

entries.tip: Save one-shot tokens (Clerk rig, Puppeteer, Mortician clean) for one decisive day when your bloc is near half, and use them together. Rig so that any nomination you can pass kills. Puppet a trusted villager to push it. That night, kill and clean the puppeted player so their will can't reveal the puppeting. Once you hold a voting majority, stop arguing and vote as a bloc. Hang the most dangerous town role first (e.g. a Veteran), then finish with the night kill.

support.note: On N5 Bob rigged D6, Olivia puppeted Niaj and Heidi was executed. Alice then killed and cleaned Niaj, leaving 3v2, and the Yakuza won. Bob, Frank, Olivia and the moderator all reported this.

entries.tip: Puppet the most trusted confirmed villager (e.g. an Oracle-confirmed role) on the day you need a swing, ideally the same Day as a Clerk rig. Their word moves undecided players. Kill them that night, and have the Mortician clean them, before they can expose the puppeting.

support.note: Olivia puppeted Niaj, whom an Oracle had confirmed as Ex-Con, to push the D6 hang. Niaj was killed and cleaned on N6.

entries.tip: If you're told you are puppeted, write it in your last will at once; expect to be killed that night. Name whoever immediately backed your puppet's push as the likely Puppeteer. Your votes are still your own, so vote by your own reads. Town: a confirmed player who suddenly pushes out of character may be puppeted.

support.note: Niaj's will exposing the puppeting was hidden by Alice's clean, so the town never learned it.

entries.tip: Agree on votes in night chat, but give each teammate a different argument in their own wording, or have one vote silently. Near-identical justifications posted back to back read as a night-chat script. Don't have one teammate open with a one-line nomination that the others echo.

support.note: Alice and Bob: the town called out their matching wording. Judy, Mallory and Erin cited it as a team tell.

entries.tip: If you have innate Defense and survive a night attack, nobody else knows who the target was, so deny being attacked. Admitting survival as a claimed Vanilla points straight at innate Defense. If you must explain it, choose one consistent claim at once (e.g. Medic who self-protected). Never switch claims under pressure.

support.note: Heidi went from 'VV, thanks Medic' to 'Medic' on trial and was hanged.

entries.tip: As a solo killer, watch for players who vote together on every key hang, defended a flipped Yakuza and lead pushes on proven town roles. Douse or kill them first: removing the Yakuza leaves a town you can outlast, and one ignite can hit the whole bloc.

support.note: Heidi correctly doused Alice, Bob and Olivia, all Yakuza, but never ignited.

entries.tip: Alert on the nights you are most likely to be visited: right after you drew attention, defended someone or made a bait claim. A quiet investigator-style claim can bait the Katana onto your alert night. Don't burn tokens on quiet nights.

support.note: Carol alerted on N3, N4 and N6 with no visitors, which gave the Village nothing.

entries.tip: On Day 1, power roles (Party Animal, investigators) should avoid being the voice that steers discussion or calls out quiet players. The most leader-like voice is a common first Katana target. Save your influence for when you have information.

support.note: Dave led Day 1 and was the N1 kill. Thin, single report.

entries.tip: Before each night, write your planned target into your will (e.g. 'N2 plan: audit X'), so your death still yields info. Label it as a plan and hedge accusations: a will can't be updated after death, and a confident line can hang a villager. Town: a will's 'plan' is not proof the action happened, since players switch targets.

support.note: Dave died N1 with an empty will. Erin's will line 'Ivan is very suspicious' helped hang the real Philanthropist. Ivan's plan will was then used in FT count math against him.

entries.tip: Survey-style or role results that keep matching claims and flips don't verify the claimer. A Yakuza Diviner publishes real reads on non-teammates and invents 'clears' for teammates. Trust only results that revealed something nobody had said yet, and require an independent check (Oracle guess, Accountant audit). When such a claimer flips Yakuza, re-examine everyone they cleared, but don't hang their true reads' subjects just for being 'confirmed' by them.

support.note: Frank, a Diviner posing as Surveyor, fooled the town for three days. Grace, Ivan, Mallory, Judy and Niaj all reported this.

entries.tip: Fake-claim a role whose results look like yours, such as Surveyor. Divine teammates who must visit risky targets: Strong Defense stops traps and Vigilante shots, and the visit can be published as a fake survey. Mix in at least one harmless unconfirmable result so a Roleplayer fallback stays believable. Remember an Accountant sees you at 0 tokens, and a gifted token is thrown away.

support.note: Frank's Surveyor cover held three days and he divined Bob (the Katana holder) on N3. It broke to Erin's Oracle WRONG, and Grace's 0-token audit would have exposed it too.

entries.tip: Audit the newest claimed token role (Surveyor, Philanthropist, Medic) early; Yakuza fake token roles to explain Diviner-style results. Work out the expected count first (start tokens, spends, gifts) so you can act on the result immediately. Don't announce the audit or PM the claimer.

support.note: Grace audited Frank to 0 tokens but was killed before she could report it.

entries.tip: Guess the public role claims of suspicious or load-bearing players: trusted investigators, defenders of flipped Yakuza and cheap VV claims. A WRONG exposes a fake at once, and a RIGHT clears them. Confirming an already-harmless claim gains little. Once confirmed, assume you die tonight and keep your will hedged.

support.note: Erin's WRONG on Frank = Surveyor got Frank hanged as a Diviner. Her RIGHT on Niaj = Ex-Con gained little.

entries.tip: Give tokens only to roles verified by something other than their own claim, and never announce whom you plan to gift. You're never told if the token was thrown away, so a fake claimer can just 'confirm' the gift, and your credibility gets tied to theirs.

support.note: Ivan announced a survey token for Frank. Frank 'confirmed' it, and once Frank flipped Diviner, Ivan looked like his partner and was hanged.

entries.tip: On trial, lead with one concrete, checkable alternative explanation of the evidence, e.g. the exact visit assignment that fits the numbers. A counter-accusation reads as deflection; a worked example that collapses the case can move votes.

support.note: Ivan's reflection on his hanging over FT counts.

entries.tip: Never narrow down your trap's location, in public or private ('not on X, Y'); a PM exchange with one player also hints the trap is there. You can't trap yourself, so once identified you're a safe kill. Stay unidentified as long as you can and let the trap's mere existence deter.

support.note: Mallory's exclusions let the Yakuza route kills around her trap. The trap only fired on the final night.

entries.tip: Track where a Trapper's trap could be: every visit that doesn't kill rules a player out, and the Trapper's PM partners are likely spots. Avoid visiting the likely trapped player, or have the Diviner give the holder Strong Defense, until the winning night. Night deaths are checked together, so a killing blow still wins even if the holder dies; give that last Katana to the least useful teammate.

support.note: Mallory's trap killed Alice on the final night, too late. Alice, Bob, Frank and Olivia all reported this.

entries.tip: Against a Fortune Teller, choose the Katana holder so the night's visits match your team's public claims. A holder whose own action hits the kill target counts as one visitor. Plan the visitor and target counts each night; unexplained extras give the town 'hidden visitor' evidence.

support.note: Alice, Olivia and the moderator: the holders were chosen deliberately, and Judy's counts fit the Yakuza stories.

entries.tip: Don't vouch for other players in your last will unless something independent of their own claims verified them. A dead player's endorsement carries extra weight and props up a Yakuza.

support.note: Mallory's reflection on the trusted fake claims.

entries.tip: Estimate the Yakuza count early (about 4 in a 13-player game). Before each late-game hang, count the worst case: if every unconfirmed Guilty voter could be Yakuza, a mis-hang may hand them the win. Push hangs on the suspected bloc while the Village still holds the majority.

support.note: Judy, Grace and Niaj: the Ivan mis-hang at 7 alive let three coordinated Yakuza votes decide the rest of the game.
